title: Company OKR Binding Map & Cross-Functional Commitment Protocol
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Purpose: Create a single-source-of-truth ‘Binding Map’ that explicitly ties every company-level OKR to the set of cross-functional initiatives and team commitments required to deliver it. This ticket defines the protocol for how teams commit capacity to OKRs, how mid-cycle rebalance requests are triaged, and how we reconcile delivery variance into the company roadmap.

Scope: Company-level OKRs (all pillars) and all initiatives that claim >5% capacity from any org. Includes: mapping template, commitment ledger, rebalance policy, escalation ladder, acceptance criteria, and tooling hooks for the Console and Planning dashboards. Excludes team-level sprint plans.

Why now: Past quarters showed blurred ownership between Platform and Runtime on cost/latency OKRs. We need a repeatable protocol so engineering, product, and design can make binding commitments with predictable escalation paths.

Desired outcomes:
  - A machine-readable Binding Map that can be surfaced in the Console and used by growth and sales for customer communications.
  - A commitment protocol that limits mid-quarter scope drift while enabling priority shifts under defined conditions.
  - Clear handoffs and SLA expectations for initiative owners and operational teams.

Primary stakeholders: PMs (company and initiative), Eng leads for serving runtime, Platform, DX, Design lead for initiative UX, Customer Success for comms.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Binding Map template published in Confluence and JSON schema checked into infra repo.
2) Minimum viable ledger UI spec accepted by Design and Product.
3) Rebalance policy ratified with exec sign-off and documented escalation ladder.
4) Two pilot initiatives (runtime perf and console rollouts) onboarded to the map and used during weekly synapse calls.
5) Dashboard shows per-initiative committed FTE% and remaining risk score in planning view.

Milestone 1 (2025-02-17): Draft Binding Map schema + template.
Milestone 2 (2025-02-24): Rebalance policy draft + escalation ladder.
Milestone 3 (2025-03-10): Design mockups for ledger UI + review.
Milestone 4 (2025-03-24): Engineering infra for JSON schema + Console hooks (API contract).
Milestone 5 (2025-04-07): Pilot two initiatives + retrospective.
Milestone 6 (2025-04-18): Finalize playbook and roll out company-wide.
decision_log:
2025-02-11: Decided Binding Map will use percentage capacity commitments (FTE%) rather than story points to standardize across orgs.
2025-02-13: Agreed on three allowed mid-quarter rebalance reasons: critical customer escalations, security incidents, and exec-prioritized strategic shifts (>10% company priority).
2025-02-14: Selected escalation ladder: Initiative Lead -> PM Synapse -> Product Directors -> CRO/CTO for final trade-offs.
risks_mitigations:
Risk: Teams will over-commit to multiple OKRs leading to unrealistic plans. Mitigation: Ledger enforces an org-level capacity cap and flags >85% committed.
Risk: Tooling lag prevents real-time visibility. Mitigation: Start with weekly uploads and dashboard sync; schedule infra sprint for automation Q3.
Risk: Cultural resistance to binding commitments. Mitigation: Pilot two initiatives and present quantitative outcomes in retros to drive adoption.
sync_process:
Weekly 'OKR Synapse' meeting: 30 minutes, PM-led. Agenda: commit deltas, open rebalance requests, blockers, and risk score changes. Monthly cross-org review with exec sponsors for any escalations. Ad-hoc emergency synapse for security or customer incidents. Meeting notes stored under Confluence > Company OKR Binding Map.
The protocol: any rebalance request must include impact statement, alternate mitigation options, and proposed owners for follow-through.

open_questions:
1) How should external partners' contributions be represented (vendor-managed vs Redwood-managed)?
2) Do we require legal sign-off for any commitments that affect customer SLAs?
3) Should rolling forecasts be allowed (e.g., monthly re-estimates) or only discrete rebalance events?
post_mortem_template: For pilot retros: Include baseline committed vs delivered FTE%, realized impact on OKR metric, variance root cause, and recommended process changes. Store under Confluence and link to retro in the ledger entry.
communication_plan: Pre-launch: Announce charter in All-Hands and post Confluence summary. During pilot: Weekly synapse notes + exec sponsorship updates. Post-rollout: Training sessions for PMs and Eng leads and a short 'how-to' video recorded by DevRel. Customer-facing comms: CS will use dashboard exports for monthly updates to top 10 customers impacted by cost/latency improvements.
